European founding — founder and leadership backgrounds¶

Purpose¶

We describe where European-founded companies in this sample find their leaders—schools, prior employers, time in the workforce before joining the company, and how first versus highest qualifications differ before the company’s founding year (from your company file). Together, this answers whether talent pipelines look stable or shifting across cohorts.

Who is in each view¶

Results are shown separately for:

  1. Unicorns founded in or before 2022 — co-founders
  2. Unicorns from 2023 onward — senior executive team (where that roster applies)
  3. Unicorns from 2023 onward — matched co-founders from your list
  4. All founders and co-founders combined (items 1 and 3 together, not the executive-only roster)

“Europe founding” here means the company is not classified as founded in Israel in this dataset; other geographies in range are treated as Europe for this slice.

How to read the visuals¶

Four-panel work chart

  • Schools: first bachelor-level school on file, using dated education rows on or before the founding year.
  • Employers: prior employers, rolled up to a group level where possible so brands sit under one corporate name.
  • People by country: how many distinct people sit under each founding-country label in the slice.
  • Tenure before joining the company: time in relevant roles before first joining this company; country averages only appear where there are enough people that the average is not dominated by one or two profiles.

Degree mix — two versions

  • Highest qualification before founding: among dated education that ends on or before the founding year (or starts there if an end date is missing), we take each person’s top degree category.
  • First qualification before founding: among those same pre-founding rows, we take the earliest dated credential. When the two diverge, it often reflects returning to study later in career (for example, a master’s or doctorate after a first bachelor’s).

Field of study

The same “first vs highest before founding” idea is applied to field / major, where populated.

Tables (after the charts)¶

You will see ranked employers, schools by founding country, and a short numeric summary of time in the workforce before joining the company. These mirror the charts and are suitable for appendices or footnotes.

Interpreting differences (carefully)¶

  • Cohorts are not interchangeable: executive samples and founder samples are built differently; contrasts are descriptive, not proof of hiring “better” or “worse” profiles.
  • Coverage gaps (missing degrees or dates) are normal; they can shift shares slightly between cohorts.
  • First vs highest degree: large moves usually mean more mid-career education in one cohort than another—not a simple quality ranking.

European founding — scope of this section¶

This section adds a Europe-only founding view of the same themes as the main analysis: schools, prior employers, tenure before joining the company, and education mix (degree level and field).

  • Geography: companies whose founding country is treated as Europe in this dataset (Israel is excluded from this slice).
  • Employers: names are shown at group level where possible.
  • Schools: each person’s first bachelor-level school, using education rows on or before the founding year.
  • Tenure: cumulative years in relevant roles before first joining the portfolio company, using the same role-quality filters as elsewhere in the analysis.
  • People in scope: founders and co-founders for unicorns through 2022, plus 2023 onward matched co-founders, and an all-founders combination; one block shows the 2023 onward executive team separately where that roster applies.

The charts and tables that follow are the numerical outputs for those cohorts under the Europe founding filter.

Europe · Unicorn year ≤2022 — co-founders — first vs final degree (insights)¶

  • Pre-founding filter: only education rows whose end year (EDU_END / ENDDATE) fall on or before the CSV UNICORN_YEAR_FOUNDED are kept; if end date is missing, the start year must be on or before that founding year. Rows without a parseable founding year from the join are excluded from these mixes.

  • Final / highest (pre-founding) = among those rows, the highest degree bucket still observed before founding. - First dated (pre-founding) = among those rows, the earliest dated credential before founding.

  • Final / highest (top buckets): Master 46.1%, Bachelor 28.9%, MBA 16.8%

  • First dated (top buckets): Bachelor 51.6%, Master 32.6%, High School 7.1%

  • Bachelor: first-dated 51.6% vs final/highest 28.9% (Δ -22.7 points) — often driven by later graduate study after the first credential.

  • Master: first-dated 32.6% vs final/highest 46.1% (Δ +13.5 points) — often driven by later graduate study after the first credential.

  • MBA: first-dated 6.5% vs final/highest 16.8% (Δ +10.3 points) — often driven by later graduate study after the first credential.

  • Doctorate: first-dated 1.6% vs final/highest 7.8% (Δ +6.2 points) — often driven by later graduate study after the first credential.
